labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it is.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 12 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at
least)
   line 59:  p300.aspirate(12, tuberack["A3"])
   At line 59 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 12 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul. A
   pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and
   the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells:
   tube A3 in slot 2.
   Affected: tube A3 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

7. WARNING MIX-BEFORE-DRAW: Liquid drawn from tube A2 in slot 2 before it was mixed: added
at line 65, drawn at line 78
   line 65:  p300.dispense(12, tuberack["A2"])
   At line 65 liquid was added to tube A2 in slot 2, which already held a different liquid.
   At line 78 liquid was drawn out of it again, and the well was never mixed in between. Two
   liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the tip drew is not at
   the concentration you calculated. In a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: tube A2 in slot 2.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix the well after the addition at line 65: `mix_after=(5, volume)` in a transfer,
   or `pipette.mix(5, volume, well)`. Integra suggests about 5 cycles at about 80% of the
   volume in the well.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide

8. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
   line 79:  p300.dispense(2.5, plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 79 the robot put polymerase into wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more
   in slot 3 (this line did it 11 times). Take well A1 in slot 3: at that moment it held
   only 10 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 82, to make the
   20.5 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol
   and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have
   brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets
   many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star
   activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3:
   water and buffer first, then the sample, then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of
   water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html

   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [a711be22277b]

9. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (tube A5 in slot 2)
   line 81:  p300.aspirate(10.5, tuberack["A5"])
   At line 81 the tip went into water (tube A5 in slot 2) while it still carried buffer
   (tube A1 in slot 2), polymerase (tube A2 in slot 2), fwd primer (tube A3 in slot 2) and
   rev primer (tube A4 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid
   leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material
   that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along
   into 2 other wells: tube C5 in slot 2; well A12 in slot 3.
   Affected: tube A5 in slot 2.
   Also reached 2 other wells: tube C5 in slot 2; well A12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 81 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling

12. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 11 wells of polymerase with a sample
   line 79:  p300.dispense(2.5, plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 79 the robot starts putting polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot
   3), and 11 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the
   mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated,
   or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate
   can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in
   slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.5 ul of polymerase and 2 ul of water in place
   of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [8fb961c5cb47]

13. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 12 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4
and 8 more went in (8 to 9% of the well)
   line 85:  p300.dispense(2, plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 85 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 8 more to wells A1,
   A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3, which already held buffer, polymerase,
   fwd primer, rev primer and 1 more (this line did it 12 times). The addition was 8 to 9%
   of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two
   liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before
   cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3 after line 85:
   `mix_after=(5, 18 to 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 18 to 20, well)`, with the
   volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to

findings.title: 12 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
findings.explanation: At line 59 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 12 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul. A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: tube A3 in slot 2.
findings.fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

findings.title: Liquid drawn from tube A2 in slot 2 before it was mixed: added at line 65, drawn at line 78
findings.explanation: At line 65 liquid was added to tube A2 in slot 2, which already held a different liquid. At line 78 liquid was drawn out of it again, and the well was never mixed in between. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the tip drew is not at the concentration you calculated. In a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
findings.fix: Mix the well after the addition at line 65: `mix_after=(5, volume)` in a transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, volume, well)`. Integra suggests about 5 cycles at about 80% of the volume in the well.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
findings.explanation: At line 79 the robot put polymerase into wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3 (this line did it 11 times). Take well A1 in slot 3: at that moment it held only 10 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 82, to make the 20.5 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3: water and buffer first, then the sample, then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: water (tube A5 in slot 2)
findings.explanation: At line 81 the tip went into water (tube A5 in slot 2) while it still carried buffer (tube A1 in slot 2), polymerase (tube A2 in slot 2), fwd primer (tube A3 in slot 2) and rev primer (tube A4 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 2 other wells: tube C5 in slot 2; well A12 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 81 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: 12 stocks
findings.explanation: At line 84 the tip went into sample 1 (tube A6 in slot 2), sample 2 (tube B1 in slot 2), sample 3 (tube B2 in slot 2), sample 4 (tube B3 in slot 2) and 8 more while it still carried buffer (tube A1 in slot 2), polymerase (tube A2 in slot 2), fwd primer (tube A3 in slot 2), rev primer (tube A4 in slot 2) and 1 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 84 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: No no-template control: 11 wells of polymerase with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 79 the robot starts putting polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3), and 11 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.5 ul of polymerase and 2 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 12 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 8 more went in (8 to 9% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 85 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 8 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3, which already held buffer, polymerase, fwd primer, rev primer and 1 more (this line did it 12 times). The addition was 8 to 9% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3 after line 85: `mix_after=(5, 18 to 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 18 to 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
